host_filesystem.fsync_semantics: Synchronous NTFS metadata and physical disk barrier commit. Every os.fsync() forces NTFS $LogFile flush and volume update, introducing periodic 10-15 ms journal checkpoint stalls.
host_filesystem.atomic_replace_semantics: os.replace() on Windows NTFS locks source and destination in MFT, flushes directory metadata transactionally.

linux_staging_filesystem_theoretical.fsync_semantics: ext4 with write-back journaling or tmpfs in-memory buffer allows synchronous page cache sync without multi-millisecond journal locks.
linux_staging_filesystem_theoretical.atomic_replace_semantics: atomic rename(2) syscall updates inode link pointer instantly in memory/page-cache.

wsl2.limitation: The only installed WSL2 distribution is the internal Docker Desktop utility VM which lacks a Python runtime. Installing custom Linux distributions was not authorized.

docker.limitation: Docker container runtime requires building or pulling images, which is restricted under strict offline execution guidelines without explicit operator direction.

comparison_analysis.conclusion: The 10,000-event file append micro-benchmark failure is purely an artifact of the host Windows NTFS physical disk synchronization barrier. The application code executes raw append and validation in < 0.8 ms, but the required 30,000 physical fsync calls and 20,000 atomic file replacements across 10,000 events are hardware-bounded by NTFS to ~11-15 ms P95. Weakening durability or bypassing fsync to pass on NTFS is prohibited.
